title.narrative: Communal Climate Action and Landscape Management Project

description.narrative: The development objective of Communal Climate Action and Landscape Management Project is to strengthen sustainable landscape management and improve income generation in targeted forest areas in Burkina Faso. This project has four components. The first component, Decentralized management of natural resources, has the following sub-components: Strategic land use planning and management; and : Investments in agro-sylvo-pastoral communal landscapes. The second component, : Institutional strengthening for integrated landscape management, environmental and social risk management, and mobilization of climate finance, has the following sub-components: Intersectoral harmonization, coordination and capacity building for integrated landscape management; Strengthening country systems for environmental and social risk management; and Enabling environment for mobilizing climate finance. The third component, Entrepreneurship and sustainable development of value chains, has the following sub-components: Sustainable development of shea, moringa and other green economy value chains; and Support for cooperatives and SMEs in targeted municipalities. The fourth component, Project coordination, monitoring and evaluation, has the following sub-components: Administration, coordination and project management; and Monitoring and evaluation (M&E), communication and knowledge management.
To strengthen sustainable landscape management and improve income generation in targeted forest areas in Burkina Faso.

condition.narrative: Section I.A.1(a). The Recipient shall maintain at all times during Project implementation, a Project review committee (“ReviewCommittee”) for the Project, with a composition, mandate and resources satisfactory to the Association.

Section I.A.2. The Recipient shall maintain at all times during Project implementation, the Director General of the Green Economyand Climate Change under the MTEE, acting as National Project Coordinator and responsible for Project oversight.

Section I.A.3(d). Not later than thirty (30) days from the Effective Date, or any later date agreed by the Association, theRecipient shall establish and thereafter maintain four (4) regional Project implementation regional branches to support theimplementation and coordination of Project activities in the regions and municipalities selected to participate in the Project, allwith qualifications, experience and terms of reference satisfactory to the Association.

Section I.A.3. (a) The Recipient shall maintain throughout Project implementation a Project implementation unit within the Ministryin charge of environment (“Project Implementation Unit” or “PIU”) with a composition, mandate and resources satisfactory to theAssociation.

Section I.C.1. The Recipient shall prepare and thereafter adopt, not later three (3) months after the Effective Date, or any laterdate as agreed by the Association, a project implementation manual in form and substance satisfactory to the Association.

Section I.G. The Recipient shall, and shall cause the Project Implementing Entity to, ensure that the Project is implemented inaccordance with the Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (“ESCP”), in a manner acceptable to the Association.

Section I.I. Without limitations to Section 5.03 of the General Conditions, the Recipient shall provide, or cause to be provided,promptly as needed, the funds, facilities, services and other resources: (a) required for the Project; and (b) necessary orappropriate to enable the PIU to perform its obligations under the Project.

Section IV. The Recipient shall, not later three (3) months after the Effective Date, or such later date as agreed by theAssociation, customize the accounting software in form and substance satisfactory to the Association.

Within six months of project approval, the Recipient shall carry out a risk assessment of SEA/SH and shall develop, if necessary, aresponse action plan in line with the national provisions and conventions ratified by Burkina Faso.

title.narrative: Citizens providing feedback through consultations that is integrated into project interventions

comment.narrative:
The results of the DPPs in the 60 communes of the first two waves of the project show that a total of 12,033 people, including 5,524 vulnerable people, consensually validated the investment proposals in their villages; this represents 88% achievement of the final target, compared with a forecast of 68% as of December 31, 2025.
As part of the restructuring, the target for this indicator will be maintained.
The indicator could exceed its target based on projected investments in the remaining 42 communes, particularly once the data related to the validation of investments in the 6 communes where the PDIC/REDD+ were prepared using an endogenous approach are taken into account.

During the period, 1,342 jobs were created through the implementation of the PDIC/REDD+ (139 jobs) and the subprojects (1,203 jobs); this represents 38% achievement of the final target, compared with a forecast of 57% for the period. The data relating to the subprojects concern those that were almost completed as of December 31, 2025, out of a potential for creating or improving more than 11,000 jobs. Trends are therefore favorable toward achieving the indicator target before the deadline. As part of the restructuring, the indicator will be reformulated as “number of jobs created or improved through the Project” to align with the World Bank scorecard, with “number of green jobs” becoming a sub-indicator. The initial target will be revised upward by 500 additional jobs to take into account improved jobs and the new jobs that will be created/improved through new activities with high job-creation potential.

This indicator refers to the number of individuals who have acquired a job with low GHG emissions, respectful of the environment and contributing to the fight against poverty within the framework of the implementation of the project. This will involve determining the green jobs that will be created through the implementation of the PDICs (establishment of multifunctional platforms, market gardens with boreholes, etc.) and the financing of the PDEs (strengthening of sustainable value chains in the forestry sector, support for SMEs) in the targeted municipalities.
The project will finance 499 sub-projects. The number of jobs created is expected to meet the annual target. To date, 139 jobs have been created, of which 59 are for youth.
The actual number of jobs created to date is 139 and will be updated again in January 2026 during the mid-term review.

title.narrative: Municipalities with functional local land management and land reconciliation structures

comment.narrative:
This indicator measures the number of municipalities with one or more functional local land administration structures (this includes rural land service, village land commission and village land reconciliation commission that are staffed, fully trained and are servicing community members). The Project will support their establishment or strengthening.
To date, 20 municipalities have functional local land management and land conciliation structures thanks to the project through the establishment, training, and equipping (wave 1) of 544 CFVs and 544 CCFVs; this represents a 33% achievement rate of the final target, The adoption of decrees and the establishment of new CFVs and CCFVs in 10 new municipalities are underway and will be completed in January 2026.

comment.narrative:

title.narrative: Implementation progress of Integrated Communal Development Plans

comment.narrative:
It is a criterion for monitoring the performance of the Integrated Communal Development Plans (PDIC). The overall progress index is the weighted average of the progress of activities. The progress index of an activity is the product of its physical performance rate and its theoretical weight. The weight of an activity is proportional to the share of its theoretical cost in the estimated budget of the PDIC. The overall progress index is therefore the sum of the progress indices of all activities divided by the total number of activities.
This is progress for the first wave of investments that have been effectively launched, the average progress index is estimated at 75%, with 15 communes having achieved an index of 70% or more, making them eligible to disburse an additional tranche of funds. This percentage will be updated in January 2026 during the mid-term review to also include progress on the second wave.

title.narrative: Proportion of project's physical investments registered in the land cadaster

comment.narrative:
Of the 368 sites established under the implementation of wave 1 and 2 PDIC/REDD+, 139 had been registered as of December 31, 2025; this corresponds to an achievement rate of 37%, against a forecast of 75%. In 2025, the project prioritized the registration of conservation areas over other investment sites in order first to stabilize the selection of those sites before registration.
As part of the restructuring, the initial target for the indicator will be revised downward from 75% to 60%. This reduction is due to the time constraints the project will face, given the length of time required by the land tenure security process and the expected increase in the number of investment sites as new activities are proposed.
The project could initiate the land tenure security process for all investment sites by June 2028 and would subsequently transfer the remaining backlog to DGFOMER to finalize the process for the remaining sites.

title.narrative: Proportion of project's physical investments registered in the land cadaster

comment.narrative:
The Project's physical investments is secured when the area is registered in the land cadaster on the basis of the registration (land title). This indicator measures the ratio between the number of registered investments and the total number of project investments.
75% of sites under the first wave have been registered as of now. The indicator will be further updated in January 2026 during the mid-term review.

354 people trained over the 1,701, which noted a strengthening of their capacities.

title.narrative: Improvement in the capacity of national and local authorities to manage project activities

comment.narrative:
To date, 692 of the 711 enrolled staff members have completed their training, representing an achievement rate of 97%. Implementation of the capacity-building plan will be discontinued under the project restructuring; therefore, this indicator is no longer relevant. It is proposed to reformulate the indicator as “number of staff whose technical capacities have been strengthened through the project,” with a target of 711 staff.
Seven Master's students and two doctoral students are still in training, which will ultimately make it possible to complete the value of the indicator and conclude implementation of the staff capacity-building plan.
